citation.title: A roentgenographic cephalometric study of prognathism in Chinese males and females

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08: norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 13 differences (logs/task9a2-compare-<id>.log). Every mean and SD of both extractors re-read from the page images (PDF pp. 2-6 = journal pp. 20-24), and the settled file checked by script against a third, independent reading of the pages (the table in sets.test.ts). Decisions: (0) Source text normalised to one pattern giving table, page, row and column with sex and age (a and b worded it differently; prose only). Adult rows: a gave [18, 40], b no band -> [18, 40] with the P18 note (merge notes). (1) a's U1-SN 107 ± 9 (males) rejected: Table IV p. 23 prints it in the Chan column (its left edge aligned with Chan's 84 ± 3 and 33 ± 4), not Wei's, whose column holds only SNA, SNB, ANB and S-N (b did not enter it; it is in moate2002-chan1972). Page images: PDF pp. 2-6 = journal pp. 20-24 (Tables I-VI), rendered at 2000 px.

caveats: Quoted second-hand from Moate & Darendeliler 2002 (Aust Orthod J 18:19-26, a compilation of published Chinese cephalometric norms), Table IV; the original paper was not read. The compilation rounds every mean and SD to whole numbers (Lew's soft tissue to 0.5) and gives no landmark, plane or method definitions.
The compilation states no film scale or magnification for any study; assumed true size (owner ruling M-2).

107 young adults of Chinese ethnic descent (84 male, 23 female), selected from 253 for facial harmony, no previous orthodontic treatment and Chinese descent; mean age 23 (males) and 21 (females) (text p. 20). The place is not stated.
Not entered (not catalogue measurements; no ratio computed): S-N (65 ± 3 males, 63 ± 2 females).
Table V (p. 24) averages several studies; it is not entered for this study (merge notes).
